      var MIN_VIEWABILITY = 60;

      var slotStates = new Map();

      function getSlotState(slot) {
      if (!slotStates.has(slot)) {
      slotStates.set(slot, {
      visibility: 0,
      timer: null,
      lastRenderTime: 0,
      hasFilledAd: false,
      refreshPending: false
      });
      }

      return slotStates.get(slot);
      }

      function clearSlotTimer(state) {
      if (state.timer !== null) {
      clearTimeout(state.timer);
      state.timer = null;
      }
      }

      function scheduleSlotRefresh(slot) {
      var state = getSlotState(slot);

      if (
      state.timer !== null ||
      state.refreshPending ||
      !state.hasFilledAd ||
      state.visibility < MIN_VIEWABILITY ||
      document.visibilityState !== 'visible'
      ) {
      return;
      }

      var elapsed = Date.now() - state.lastRenderTime;
      var delay = Math.max(0, REFRESH_INTERVAL - elapsed);

      // Require continuous 60% visibility for the full interval.
      state.timer = setTimeout(function () {
      state.timer = null;

      if (
      document.visibilityState !== 'visible' ||
      state.visibility < MIN_VIEWABILITY ||
      !state.hasFilledAd ||
      state.refreshPending
      ) {
      return;
      }

      // Enforce minimum interval since the last successful render.
      if (Date.now() - state.lastRenderTime < REFRESH_INTERVAL) {
      scheduleSlotRefresh(slot);
      return;
      }

      state.refreshPending = true;

      // Refresh this slot only, never all slots.
      googletag.pubads().refresh([slot]);

      }, delay);

      var state = getSlotState(slot);

      if (state.visibility >= MIN_VIEWABILITY) {
      scheduleSlotRefresh(slot);
      } else {
      // Cancel the countdown immediately when visibility drops.
      clearSlotTimer(state);
      }
      }
      );

      // Refresh only slots that have a filled ad.

      state.refreshPending = false;

      state.lastRenderTime = Date.now();

      }

<style>
    * {
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        box-sizing: border-box;
    }

    body {
        font-family: "Inter", sans-serif;
        font-size: 14px;
        color: #000;
    }

    .header {
        text-align: center;
        padding: 10px 0;
        position: relative;
    }

    .logo img {
        width: 250px;
        height: auto;
        max-width: 100%;
        display: block;
        margin: 0 auto;
    }

    .top-meta {
        font-size: .75rem;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: 1px;
    }
    nav a.activer {
        font-weight: bold;
    }

    /* Hamburger */
    .menu-toggle {
        display: none;
        position: absolute;
        top: 15px;
        right: 15px;
        font-size: 24px;
        background: none;
        border: none;
        cursor: pointer;
    }

    nav {
        border-top: 4px solid #000;
        border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;
        margin-top: 10px;
    }

    nav ul {
        display: flex;
        list-style: none;
        justify-content: center;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
        padding: 0;
    }

    nav li {
        margin: 0 8px;
    }

    nav a {
        text-decoration: none;
        color: #000;
        font-weight: 500;
        padding: 7px 6px;
        display: block;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        font-size: .9rem;
    }

    nav a.active,
    nav a:hover {
        color: #c00;
    }
    ul.main-menu {
        margin-bottom: 0;
    }

    /* Responsive */
    @media (max-width: 768px) {
        

        .menu-toggle {
            display: block;
        }

        nav ul {
            flex-wrap: wrap;
            justify-content: flex-start;
            padding: 5px;
        }

        /* Hide 6th and onward items by default */
        nav ul li:nth-child(n+6) {
            display: none;
        }

        /* When menu is active, show them */
        nav ul.active li {
            display: block;
            width: 100%;
            margin: 5px 0;
            text-align: left;
        }
        nav a.active {
            font-weight: bold;
        }

        nav ul.active {
            display: block;
        }
        nav li {
            margin: 0 8px;
            text-align: center;
            margin: 0 auto;
        }
    }
    .main-menu a {
font-family: "Inter", sans-serif;
}
</style>

                <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <p>British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's <a rel="nofollow" href="https://thecommonwealth.org/latest/commonwealth-heads-government-meeting-chogm?page=9">Commonwealth summit </a>at which he is likely ‌to face demands for <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2505635/uk-lawmakers-accuse-pm-starmer-of-silencing-nations-pushing-for-discussions-on-slavery-reparations">financial reparations</a>.</p>

<p>Writing in the <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/30/andy-burnham-call-formal-apology-britains-role-in-slave-trade"><em>Guardian</em> newspaper</a>, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.</p>

<p>"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.</p>

<p>But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.slavevoyages.org">Transatlantic Slave Trade Database</a>.</p>

<p>Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637785/king-charles-sorrow-over-slavery-faces-test-as-reparations-movement-gains-ground">King Charles,</a> who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".</p>

<p>Caribbean leaders are expected to<a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2505472/time-has-come-commonwealth-leaders-push-for-discussion-on-slavery-reparations"> press demands for reparations</a>, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.</p>

<p>Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the <em>Guardian</em> that he wanted to "launch a new drive on debt", including by helping more vulnerable countries "repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates".</p>

<p><strong>Read more:</strong> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637785/king-charles-sorrow-over-slavery-faces-test-as-reparations-movement-gains-ground">King Charles' sorrow over slavery faces test as reparations movement gains ground</a></p>

<p>Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham's ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.facebook.com/gaston.browne/posts/statement-by-the-right-honourable-gaston-browne-prime-minister-of-antigua-and-ba/1702643038101083/">Facebook post</a>: "The Caribbean's longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged."</p>

headline: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
description: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
author: Reuters
article_text:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.

But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."

From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.

Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".

Caribbean leaders are expected to press demands for reparations, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.

Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the Guardian that he wanted to "launch a new drive on debt", including by helping more vulnerable countries "repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates".

Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham's ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a Facebook post: "The Caribbean's longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged."

                <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <strong class="location-names">
                                        RAWALPIND: 
            

        </strong>
            <p>The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.</p>

<p>The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.</p>

<p><strong>Read: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2629368/afridi-alleges-police-brutality">Afridi alleges police brutality</a></p>

<p>Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.</p>

<p>According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.</p>

<p>News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, <em>The Express Tribune</em> witnessed on the site.</p>

<p>According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told <em>The Express Tribune.</em></p>

<p>Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.</p>

<p><strong>Read more: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620614/casualties-reported-after-jaac-police-clash-in-ajks-rawalakot">Casualties reported after JAAC, police clash in AJK's Rawalakot</a></p>

<p>The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.</p>

<p>The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.</p>

<p>The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.</p>

<p>In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2626643/cop-penalised-for-mistreating-citizen">mistreatment of a citizen</a> at Gujjar Khan Police Station.</p>

<p>In April, <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2600985/students-file-complaint-over-police-abuse">three students</a> accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.</p>

<p>In February, a <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2591677/cops-under-fire-for-child-torture">12-year-old boy</a> was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2592953/another-case-of-alleged-police-brutality-surfaces">RA Bazaar</a> Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2593332/burn-victim-alleges-police-abuse">fire</a> at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.</p>

headline: Rawalpindi police says legal action underway after man dies of 'police brutality' at Taxila check post
description: The victim's family says children pleaded with cops to spare the 30-year-old man, to no avail
author: Imran Asghar
article_text:
The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.

The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.

Read: Afridi alleges police brutality

Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.

According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.

News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, The Express Tribune witnessed on the site.

According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.

“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told The Express Tribune.

Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.

The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.

The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.

The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.

In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged mistreatment of a citizen at Gujjar Khan Police Station.

In April, three students accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.

In February, a 12-year-old boy was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at RA Bazaar Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on fire at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.

                <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <strong class="location-names">
                                        MIRANSHAH: 
            

        </strong>
            <p>A police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge inside the Judicial Complex in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Lakki Marwat on Saturday. </p>

<p>District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital spokesperson Jalal Khan said Constable Karamatullah was killed on the spot, while PPP District Information Secretary Advocate Javed Iqbal received bullet wounds. Another individual, identified as Inshaullah, was also wounded in the firing.</p>

<p>Both the injured were taken to Bannu for medical treatment, with Khan confirming that one body and two injured persons had been brought to the hospital for medical treatment.</p>

<p>The armed assailants reportedly opened indiscriminate fire outside the courtroom, triggering panic and prompting lawyers, litigants and other visitors to rush for safety as gunshots rang out.</p>

<p><strong>Read: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2631528/blast-in-dera-ismail-khan-kills-11-injures-30">12 killed, 35 injured as TTP strikes anti-smuggling checkpoint in K-P's DI Khan</a></p>

<p>Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the complex and initiated an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible. Authorities subsequently sealed the complex and suspended all entry and exit movements, with the area placed under heightened security.</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>The incident also raised security concerns due to the judicial complex being a sensitive government facility where lawyers, litigants, judges and members of the public visit daily.</p>

<p>Investigations were initiated to ascertain further details regarding the motive behind the attack and the identity of the assailants.</p>

<p>Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.</p>

<p><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637853/three-cops-martyred-in-k-p-attacks">A day earlier</a>, three policemen were martyred in separate incidents in K-P's Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur, while unidentified armed men abducted a head constable in Bannu.</p>

<p><strong>Read More: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637108/k-p-council-tasked-to-evict-armed-groups">K-P council tasked to evict armed groups</a></p>

<p>In Bajaur, unidentified armed men launched a late-night attack on the Salai Pati Police Post, martyring Constable Khaista Main Syed. In Bannu, unidentified gunmen opened fire on Counter-Terrorism Department Constable Sadiq Zaman, killing him on the spot.</p>

<p>In Lakki Marwat, unidentified armed men opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near a bank, martyring him.</p>

<p>K-P has faced the brunt of terrorist incidents, which <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2634328/terror-attacks-in-k-p-surge-195-since-2024">increased by 195%</a> between March 1, 2024, and September 23, 2026, while drone attacks rose sharply. 73% of terrorist attacks recorded in K-P during 2026 targeted police and security personnel.</p>

headline: Police constable martyred, two injured in firing at Lakki Marwat judicial complex
description: Injured shifted to Bannu hospital as police heighten security, initiate investigation
author: Nasruminallah
article_text:
A police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge inside the Judicial Complex in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Lakki Marwat on Saturday.

District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital spokesperson Jalal Khan said Constable Karamatullah was killed on the spot, while PPP District Information Secretary Advocate Javed Iqbal received bullet wounds. Another individual, identified as Inshaullah, was also wounded in the firing.

Both the injured were taken to Bannu for medical treatment, with Khan confirming that one body and two injured persons had been brought to the hospital for medical treatment.

The armed assailants reportedly opened indiscriminate fire outside the courtroom, triggering panic and prompting lawyers, litigants and other visitors to rush for safety as gunshots rang out.

Read: 12 killed, 35 injured as TTP strikes anti-smuggling checkpoint in K-P's DI Khan

Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the complex and initiated an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible. Authorities subsequently sealed the complex and suspended all entry and exit movements, with the area placed under heightened security.

The incident also raised security concerns due to the judicial complex being a sensitive government facility where lawyers, litigants, judges and members of the public visit daily.

Investigations were initiated to ascertain further details regarding the motive behind the attack and the identity of the assailants.

Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.

A day earlier, three policemen were martyred in separate incidents in K-P's Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur, while unidentified armed men abducted a head constable in Bannu.

In Bajaur, unidentified armed men launched a late-night attack on the Salai Pati Police Post, martyring Constable Khaista Main Syed. In Bannu, unidentified gunmen opened fire on Counter-Terrorism Department Constable Sadiq Zaman, killing him on the spot.

In Lakki Marwat, unidentified armed men opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near a bank, martyring him.

K-P has faced the brunt of terrorist incidents, which increased by 195% between March 1, 2024, and September 23, 2026, while drone attacks rose sharply. 73% of terrorist attacks recorded in K-P during 2026 targeted police and security personnel.

                <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <p>Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2636526/fo-rejects-indian-remarks-on-oic-kashmir-resolutions-raises-alarm-over-delhi-mosque-eviction-notice">Makkah alliance</a>", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.</p>

<p>Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the <em>Syrian Arab News Agency</em> (<em>SANA</em>).</p>

<p>He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.</p>

<p>The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.</p>

<p>Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.</p>

<p>Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.</p>

<p>“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.</p>

<p><strong>Read More: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637497/pakistan-brings-regional-rivals-together">Pakistan brings regional rivals together</a></p>

<p>“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.</p>

<p>Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.</p>

<p>He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.</p>

<p>Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.</p>

              } else {
                $("#commentform2637938").trigger("reset");
                $('#success2637938').show();
                $('#success2637938').delay(1500).fadeOut();

headline: Syria says discussions underway on joining Makkah Defence Alliance
description: Syrian FM says talks are underway on joining Mecca alliance with Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.

The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.

Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.

He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.

“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.

Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.

He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.

Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.

                <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <p>British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's <a rel="nofollow" href="https://thecommonwealth.org/latest/commonwealth-heads-government-meeting-chogm?page=9">Commonwealth summit </a>at which he is likely ‌to face demands for <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2505635/uk-lawmakers-accuse-pm-starmer-of-silencing-nations-pushing-for-discussions-on-slavery-reparations">financial reparations</a>.</p>

<p>Writing in the <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/30/andy-burnham-call-formal-apology-britains-role-in-slave-trade"><em>Guardian</em> newspaper</a>, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.</p>

<p>"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.</p>

<p>But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.slavevoyages.org">Transatlantic Slave Trade Database</a>.</p>

<p>Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637785/king-charles-sorrow-over-slavery-faces-test-as-reparations-movement-gains-ground">King Charles,</a> who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".</p>

<p>Caribbean leaders are expected to<a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2505472/time-has-come-commonwealth-leaders-push-for-discussion-on-slavery-reparations"> press demands for reparations</a>, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.</p>

<p>Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the <em>Guardian</em> that he wanted to "launch a new drive on debt", including by helping more vulnerable countries "repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates".</p>

<p><strong>Read more:</strong> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637785/king-charles-sorrow-over-slavery-faces-test-as-reparations-movement-gains-ground">King Charles' sorrow over slavery faces test as reparations movement gains ground</a></p>

<p>Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham's ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.facebook.com/gaston.browne/posts/statement-by-the-right-honourable-gaston-browne-prime-minister-of-antigua-and-ba/1702643038101083/">Facebook post</a>: "The Caribbean's longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged."</p>

headline: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
description: UK PM Burnham says he is 'open' to formal apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
author: Reuters
article_text:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.

But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."

From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to calls for a formal apology for Britain's historical role in slavery, ​before attending next week's Commonwealth summit at which he is likely ‌to face demands for financial reparations.

Writing in the Guardian newspaper, Burnham said Britain was "offering a structured dialogue with those affected by the transatlantic slave trade", in which at ​least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery.

"Listening to ​calls for a formal apology on behalf of the British ⁠state will form an important part of this process, and I am ​open to them," he added.

But Burnham rejected calls for financial reparations, writing: "I do ​not think that British people today can be held liable for historical wrongs, however heinous, that happened in a different age under different laws and in which they played ​no personal part."

From the 15th to the 19th century, millions of Africans ​were sold into slavery by European traders, with Britain transporting an estimated 3.2 million ‌people ⁠across the Atlantic, according to the Transatlantic Slave Trade Database.

Ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda next week, King Charles, who is touring the Caribbean, said it was "only right that we should ​acknowledge the great suffering ​and injustices of ⁠the past".

Caribbean leaders are expected to press demands for reparations, which they have often framed in terms of ​debt relief, development finance, education, healthcare and climate resilience.

Burnham ​also wrote ⁠in the Guardian that he wanted to "launch a new drive on debt", including by helping more vulnerable countries "repay over a longer time period and with better ⁠rates".

Antigua ​and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne welcomed Burnham's ​comments and proposals for practical assistance, though he added in a Facebook post: "The Caribbean's longstanding ​position on reparatory justice remains unchanged."

                <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <strong class="location-names">
                                        RAWALPIND: 
            

        </strong>
            <p>The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.</p>

<p>The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.</p>

<p><strong>Read: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2629368/afridi-alleges-police-brutality">Afridi alleges police brutality</a></p>

<p>Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.</p>

<p>According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.</p>

<p>News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, <em>The Express Tribune</em> witnessed on the site.</p>

<p>According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told <em>The Express Tribune.</em></p>

<p>Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.</p>

<p><strong>Read more: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2620614/casualties-reported-after-jaac-police-clash-in-ajks-rawalakot">Casualties reported after JAAC, police clash in AJK's Rawalakot</a></p>

<p>The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.</p>

<p>The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.</p>

<p>The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.</p>

<p>In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2626643/cop-penalised-for-mistreating-citizen">mistreatment of a citizen</a> at Gujjar Khan Police Station.</p>

<p>In April, <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2600985/students-file-complaint-over-police-abuse">three students</a> accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.</p>

<p>In February, a <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2591677/cops-under-fire-for-child-torture">12-year-old boy</a> was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2592953/another-case-of-alleged-police-brutality-surfaces">RA Bazaar</a> Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2593332/burn-victim-alleges-police-abuse">fire</a> at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.</p>

headline: Rawalpindi police says legal action underway after man dies of 'police brutality' at Taxila check post
description: The victim's family says children pleaded with cops to spare the 30-year-old man, to no avail
author: Imran Asghar
article_text:
The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.

The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.

Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.

According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.

News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, The Express Tribune witnessed on the site.

According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.

“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told The Express Tribune.

Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.

The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.

The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.

The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.

In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged mistreatment of a citizen at Gujjar Khan Police Station.

In April, three students accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.

In February, a 12-year-old boy was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at RA Bazaar Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on fire at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.

RAWALPIND:

The Rawalpindi police on Saturday initiated legal proceedings following the death of a 30-year-old man at the Gangu Police Check Post in Taxila, with a police spokesperson assuring that a fair investigation would be conducted and those responsible would be held accountable.

The incident reportedly occurred when a man, travelling from Khanpur towards Taxila, was stopped by police personnel at the Gangu checkpost for a search of his vehicle.

Read: Afridi alleges police brutality

Local residents and the victim's family alleged that the man was subjected to severe physical assault by police personnel during the search. His family claimed that the man repeatedly pleaded with the officers to stop beating him with batons, while children at the scene also cried and appealed to the police to spare him.

According to the family, the 30-year-old died at the scene as a result of the alleged police torture.

News of his death triggered protests in the area, with angry residents blocking the Taxila-Khanpur Road and surrounding police personnel, The Express Tribune witnessed on the site.

According to Rawalpindi Police Spokesperson Inspector Sajjadul Hassan, senior police officials reached the scene after the incident sparked the road blockade and widespread protest.

“Legal proceedings are underway, and the matter would be investigated on merit to apprehend those found guilty of homicide,” Inspector Hassan told The Express Tribune.

Eyewitnesses said some protesters also assaulted police officers, leaving one policeman seriously injured.

Read more: Casualties reported after JAAC, police clash in AJK's Rawalakot

The incident sparked tensions in the area, prompting senior police officials to reach the site.

The police spokesperson said the road, which had been blocked during the protest, had subsequently been reopened to traffic.

The incident comes amid a series of allegations of police brutality and misconduct reported in Rawalpindi this year. In several of these cases, police authorities announced inquiries or departmental action following complaints and the emergence of video footage. The latest incident at the Gangu checkpost in Taxila, however, has raised further questions about police conduct during roadside checks and the use of force against civilians.

In August, a police constable was suspended and issued a charge sheet following the emergence of a video showing the alleged mistreatment of a citizen at Gujjar Khan Police Station.

In April, three students accused plainclothes police personnel of assaulting them at the Dahgal checkpoint on Adiala Road before taking them to Adiala Police Post, where they were allegedly tortured and threatened with false charges. One of the students subsequently approached the Rawalpindi city police officer, seeking legal and departmental action against the officials involved.

In February, a 12-year-old boy was allegedly tortured at Rawat Police Station, prompting the suspension of three police officials and an inquiry into the incident. The same month, a resident accused personnel at RA Bazaar Police Station of torture, blackmail and extortion, while another case involved a 45-year-old man who sustained severe burn injuries after allegedly setting himself on fire at a police post. His family accused police personnel of torture, although the police disputed the allegations and said an inquiry had been initiated.

                                                                                            <strong class="location-names">
                                        MIRANSHAH: 
            

        </strong>
            <p>A police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge inside the Judicial Complex in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Lakki Marwat on Saturday. </p>

<p>District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital spokesperson Jalal Khan said Constable Karamatullah was killed on the spot, while PPP District Information Secretary Advocate Javed Iqbal received bullet wounds. Another individual, identified as Inshaullah, was also wounded in the firing.</p>

<p>Both the injured were taken to Bannu for medical treatment, with Khan confirming that one body and two injured persons had been brought to the hospital for medical treatment.</p>

<p>The armed assailants reportedly opened indiscriminate fire outside the courtroom, triggering panic and prompting lawyers, litigants and other visitors to rush for safety as gunshots rang out.</p>

<p><strong>Read: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2631528/blast-in-dera-ismail-khan-kills-11-injures-30">12 killed, 35 injured as TTP strikes anti-smuggling checkpoint in K-P's DI Khan</a></p>

<p>Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the complex and initiated an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible. Authorities subsequently sealed the complex and suspended all entry and exit movements, with the area placed under heightened security.</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>The incident also raised security concerns due to the judicial complex being a sensitive government facility where lawyers, litigants, judges and members of the public visit daily.</p>

<p>Investigations were initiated to ascertain further details regarding the motive behind the attack and the identity of the assailants.</p>

<p>Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.</p>

<p><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637853/three-cops-martyred-in-k-p-attacks">A day earlier</a>, three policemen were martyred in separate incidents in K-P's Bannu, Lakki Marwat and Bajaur, while unidentified armed men abducted a head constable in Bannu.</p>

<p><strong>Read More: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637108/k-p-council-tasked-to-evict-armed-groups">K-P council tasked to evict armed groups</a></p>

<p>In Bajaur, unidentified armed men launched a late-night attack on the Salai Pati Police Post, martyring Constable Khaista Main Syed. In Bannu, unidentified gunmen opened fire on Counter-Terrorism Department Constable Sadiq Zaman, killing him on the spot.</p>

<p>In Lakki Marwat, unidentified armed men opened fire on Constable Mumtaz near a bank, martyring him.</p>

<p>K-P has faced the brunt of terrorist incidents, which <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2634328/terror-attacks-in-k-p-surge-195-since-2024">increased by 195%</a> between March 1, 2024, and September 23, 2026, while drone attacks rose sharply. 73% of terrorist attacks recorded in K-P during 2026 targeted police and security personnel.</p>

headline: Police constable martyred, two injured in firing at Lakki Marwat judicial complex
description: Injured shifted to Bannu hospital as police heighten security, initiate investigation
author: Nasruminallah
article_text:
A police constable was martyred and two other people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the courtroom of an additional sessions judge inside the Judicial Complex in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's (K-P's) Lakki Marwat on Saturday.

District Headquarters (DHQ) Hospital spokesperson Jalal Khan said Constable Karamatullah was killed on the spot, while PPP District Information Secretary Advocate Javed Iqbal received bullet wounds. Another individual, identified as Inshaullah, was also wounded in the firing.

Both the injured were taken to Bannu for medical treatment, with Khan confirming that one body and two injured persons had been brought to the hospital for medical treatment.

The armed assailants reportedly opened indiscriminate fire outside the courtroom, triggering panic and prompting lawyers, litigants and other visitors to rush for safety as gunshots rang out.

Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the complex and initiated an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting and identify those responsible.                 <span class="story-text">
                                                                                            <p>Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the <a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2636526/fo-rejects-indian-remarks-on-oic-kashmir-resolutions-raises-alarm-over-delhi-mosque-eviction-notice">Makkah alliance</a>", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.</p>

<p>Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the <em>Syrian Arab News Agency</em> (<em>SANA</em>).</p>

<p>He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.</p>

<p>The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.</p>

<p>Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.</p><div id='div-gpt-story-2'><script>googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.display('div-gpt-story-2'); });</script></div></p>

<p>He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.</p>

<p>Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.</p>

<p>“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.</p>

<p><strong>Read More: </strong><a rel="nofollow" href="https://tribune.com.pk/story/2637497/pakistan-brings-regional-rivals-together">Pakistan brings regional rivals together</a></p>

<p>“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.</p>

<p>Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.</p>

<p>He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.</p>

<p>Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.</p>

headline: Syria says discussions underway on joining Makkah Defence Alliance
description: Syrian FM says talks are underway on joining Mecca alliance with Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
author: Anadolu Agency
article_text:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.

The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.

Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.

He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.

“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.

Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.

He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.

Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.

article_html:
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway to evaluate Syria's entry into the Makkah alliance", a regional pact that brings together Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

Shaibani’s remarks came during a regional security session at the Manama Dialogue 2026, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

He said Damascus was an "integral" part of regional security and would support any framework aimed at protecting regional stability.

The minister stressed that the region was "in greater need than ever" of developing joint deterrence and defence systems.

Addressing the conflict in Yemen, Shaibani reaffirmed Syria's support for the Yemeni government in restoring its sovereignty and stability across the country.

He also urged all parties to support the unity and sovereignty of states.

Separately, the Syrian foreign minister said Israel has carried out more than 1,000 attacks on his country in less than two years, killing dozens of people.

“Our territory has been subjected to more than 1,000 Israeli attacks in less than two years, killing dozens.

Read More: Pakistan brings regional rivals together

“How can calls for border control and placing weapons exclusively under state control be justified while Syrian sovereignty is violated and targeted on a daily basis?” he asked.

Condemning the Israeli attacks, Shaibani called for a return to the lines in place before December 8, 2024, and implementation of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement.

He stressed that the Golan Heights is Syrian territory and that UN Security Council Resolution 497 serves as the reference on this matter.

Since the fall of the Assad regime in Syria on Dec 8, 2024, Israel has occupied the Syrian buffer zone established under the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and set up military positions inside and outside it, a move the UN described as a violation of the agreement.
